sintoma: NOC-2505: após change, CPU alta, MAC flapping VLAN 50, usuários offline. Dois trunks paralelos no access.
cli_output:
SW-ACC# show run | include spanning-tree vlan 50
no spanning-tree vlan 50

SW-ACC# show mac address-table dynamic vlan 50 | count
% high move count / flapping between Gi1/0/47 and Gi1/0/48 (ops note)

SW-ACC# show interfaces Gi1/0/47 status
Gi1/0/47  UPLINK-A  connected  trunk a-full a-1000
SW-ACC# show interfaces Gi1/0/48 status
Gi1/0/48  UPLINK-B  connected  trunk a-full a-1000

SW-DIST# show spanning-tree vlan 50
% Spanning tree instance(s) for vlan does not exist. / or STP off on peer for vlan 50

Log users: broadcast storm / network slow
Change ticket: 'disabled STP on vlan 50 to fix blocked port complaints'
alternativas: Reabilitar spanning-tree na VLAN 50 e deixar o STP bloquear um path — loops com dois trunks ativos
Manter STP off e adicionar mais um trunk
Só aumentar a priority para 61440 em todos
Só configurar BPDU Guard nos uplinks e manter STP off
explicacao_profunda: no spanning-tree vlan 50 com dois uplinks connected cria loop L2 (flapping/storm). A correção é reabilitar STP e aceitar o bloqueio de um path. Mais trunks sem STP piora. BPDU Guard nos uplinks não substitui a árvore.

sintoma: NOC-3201: site stub — LAN 10.40.0.0/24 ok; Internet e redes remotas unreachable. Sem IGP.
cli_output:
EDGE# show ip route
Codes: C - connected, S - static, R - RIP, M - mobile, B - BGP
       D - EIGRP, O - OSPF, IA - OSPF inter area
Gateway of last resort is not set

      10.0.0.0/8 is variably subnetted, 2 subnets, 2 masks
C        10.40.0.0/24 is directly connected, Vlan40
L        10.40.0.1/32 is directly connected, Vlan40
C        203.0.113.0/30 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/0/1
L        203.0.113.2/32 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/0/1

EDGE# show run | include ip route
 (no ip route commands)

EDGE# show ip interface brief | include Vlan40|Gi0/0/1
Vlan40                 10.40.0.1       YES NVRAM  up    up
GigabitEthernet0/0/1   203.0.113.2     YES NVRAM  up    up

PC 10.40.0.50: ping 10.40.0.1 OK; ping 8.8.8.8 FAIL (network unreachable on EDGE traceroute)
alternativas: Falta default route (ou statics remotas) — configurar ip route 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0 203.0.113.1
Máscara da LAN está errada no SVI
explicacao_profunda: Gateway of last resort is not set e só há C/L: sem S* para Internet. LAN e WAN links estão up. Adicione default via CE 203.0.113.1. PortFast/OSPF não explicam a tabela vazia de remotas.

sintoma: NOC-3202: desenho pedia floating backup; a rota de ‘backup’ nunca fica de reserva — às vezes compete com a primária.
cli_output:
R1# show run | include ip route 10.20.0.0
ip route 10.20.0.0 255.255.0.0 10.0.0.2
ip route 10.20.0.0 255.255.0.0 10.0.0.6 1

R1# show ip route 10.20.0.0
S        10.20.0.0/16 [1/0] via 10.0.0.2
                      [1/0] via 10.0.0.6

R1# show ip interface brief | include 10.0.0.
GigabitEthernet0/0/0   10.0.0.1    YES NVRAM  up  up
GigabitEthernet0/0/1   10.0.0.5    YES NVRAM  up  up

Design intent: primary via 10.0.0.2 AD1; backup via 10.0.0.6 only if primary fails
alternativas: Backup também com AD 1 — não é floating; subir AD do backup (ex. 210) para só assumir se a primária cair
explicacao_profunda: Duas statics com AD 1 instalam ambas (ECMP/candidates iguais). Floating exige AD maior no backup. Corrija para ip route ... 10.0.0.6 210. Links estão up.

sintoma: NOC-3203: após queda do link WAN primário, a static some e o site fica sem rota; floating configurada não aparece.
cli_output:
EDGE# show run | include ip route
ip route 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0 203.0.113.1
ip route 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0 198.51.100.1 200

EDGE# show ip interface brief | include Gi0/0/1|Gi0/0/2
GigabitEthernet0/0/1   203.0.113.2     YES NVRAM  down  down
GigabitEthernet0/0/2   198.51.100.2    YES NVRAM  down  down

EDGE# show ip route static
 (empty / no S*)

EDGE# show ip route
Gateway of last resort is not set
C    10.40.0.0/24 is directly connected, Vlan40

Ops: secondary circuit also down (fiber cut both); floating next-hop 198.51.100.1 not reachable
alternativas: Default route não existe no running-config
Ambos next-hops/interfaces down — rotas static não instalam; floating só assume se o backup path estiver up
Precisa de OSPF para floating funcionar
explicacao_profunda: Config tem primária e floating, mas Gi0/0/1 e Gi0/0/2 down: nenhum next-hop usable. Floating não é mágica sem circuito backup up. OSPF não é requisito. Levante o path 198.51.100.0/30.

sintoma: NOC-3204: rota estática ‘para o DC 10.50.1.0’ não leva ao host 10.50.2.20.
cli_output:
R1# show run | include ip route 10.50
ip route 10.50.1.0 255.255.255.0 10.0.0.2

R1# show ip route 10.50.2.20
% Network not in table

R1# show ip route 10.50.1.0
S        10.50.1.0/24 [1/0] via 10.0.0.2

R1# show ip route static
S        10.50.1.0/24 [1/0] via 10.0.0.2

PC: ping 10.50.2.20 FAIL; traceroute stops at R1 (no route)
Design doc: DC servers live in 10.50.0.0/16 (includes .1 and .2 subnets)
alternativas: Máscara/prefixo errado — /24 10.50.1.0 não cobre 10.50.2.20; usar 10.50.0.0 255.255.0.0 ou rota específica /24 de .2
explicacao_profunda: Network not in table para 10.50.2.20 com static só de 10.50.1.0/24 prova cobertura insuficiente. Ajuste o prefixo ao desenho /16 ou adicione 10.50.2.0/24. AD/exit-if não expandem a máscara.

sintoma: NOC-3205: static via exit-interface Gi0/0/0 sem next-hop; comportamento estranho de ARP e encaminhamento no multiacesso.
cli_output:
R1# show run | include ip route 172.16
ip route 172.16.0.0 255.255.0.0 GigabitEthernet0/0/0

R1# show ip route 172.16.0.0
S        172.16.0.0/16 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/0/0

R1# show ip interface brief | include Gi0/0/0
GigabitEthernet0/0/0   10.0.0.1   YES NVRAM  up  up

R1# show run interface Gi0/0/0
 ip address 10.0.0.1 255.255.255.0
 description LAN-SEGMENT-MULTIACCESS

R2 (same LAN) is 10.0.0.2 — intended next-hop to reach 172.16.0.0/16
Ops note: proxy-ARP load / incomplete ARPs for remote destinations observed
alternativas: Preferir next-hop 10.0.0.2 (ou exit-if + next-hop) em Ethernet multiacesso em vez de só exit-interface
Remover a static e usar só MAC table
explicacao_profunda: A rota aparece ‘directly connected’ via Gi0/0/0 sem next-hop — típico de static só com exit-if, com riscos de proxy ARP no multiacesso. O desenho queria 10.0.0.2. Reescreva ip route 172.16.0.0 255.255.0.0 10.0.0.2.

sintoma: NOC-3301: R1 e R2 não formam neighbor no link de campus. Hellos não estabelecem FULL.
cli_output:
R1# show ip ospf interface GigabitEthernet0/0/0 | include Area|Network Type|Hello|Dead|MTU
  Network Type BROADCAST, Cost: 1
  Topology-MTID    Cost    Disabled    Shutdown      Topology Name
  Transmit Delay is 1 sec, State DR, Priority 1
  Hello 10, Dead 40
  Area 0
  MTU is 1500

R2# show ip ospf interface GigabitEthernet0/0/0 | include Area|Network Type|Hello|Dead|MTU
  Network Type BROADCAST, Cost: 1
  Hello 10, Dead 40
  Area 1
  MTU is 1500

R1# show ip ospf neighbor
(no neighbors)

R2# show run interface Gi0/0/0 | include ospf

R1# show run interface Gi0/0/0 | include ospf
 ip ospf 1 area 0
alternativas: Area mismatch (0 vs 1) — alinhar area-id no link para single-area/adjacência
Falta de voice vlan no WAN
explicacao_profunda: Area 0 no R1 e area 1 no R2 no mesmo link impedem adjacência. Timers e MTU batem. Corrija para a mesma area. Não há evidência de RID duplicado nem de voice na WAN.

Neighbor ID     Pri   State           Dead Time   Address         Interface
2.2.2.2           0   EXSTART/  -     00:00:35    10.0.0.2        Gi0/0/1

R2# show ip ospf neighbor
Neighbor ID     Pri   State           Dead Time   Address         Interface
1.1.1.1           0   EXSTART/  -     00:00:32    10.0.0.1        Gi0/0/1

sintoma: NOC-3304: adjacências instáveis após clone de config; dois routers com o mesmo RID.

R2# show ip ospf

R3# show ip ospf neighbor
Neighbor ID     Pri State   Dead Time Address       Interface
10.10.10.10       1 FULL/DR 00:00:35  10.0.0.1      Gi0/0/0
10.10.10.10       1 FULL/BDR 00:00:33 10.0.0.2      Gi0/0/0
%OSPF-4-DUP_RTRID_AREA: Detected router with duplicate router ID

R2# show run | include router-id

explicacao_profunda: Log DUP_RTRID e mesmo process ID 10.10.10.10 em R1/R2 são RID duplicado. Use RID alinhado às loopbacks distintas e clear process com cuidado. Não mantenha duplicata.

sintoma: NOC-3305: IPv4 entre filiais ok via OSPFv2 FULL; hosts IPv6 não roteiam. R1/R2 dual-stack.

R1# show ip ospf neighbor
Neighbor ID  State    Address     Interface
2.2.2.2      FULL/  - 10.0.0.2    Gi0/0/1

R1# show ipv6 ospf neighbor
% OSPFv3 is not running ou empty table

R1# show run interface Gi0/0/1
interface GigabitEthernet0/0/1
 ip address 10.0.0.1 255.255.255.252
 ip ospf 1 area 0
 ipv6 address 2001:db8:0:12::1/64
 (no ipv6 ospf / ospfv3 command)

(no OSPF routes)

R1# show run | include ipv6 unicast|ipv6 router ospf|router ospfv3

RID IPv6 /128 obrigatório no lugar do 32-bit
explicacao_profunda: IPv6 na interface sem ospfv3/ipv6 ospf e neighbor v3 vazio explicam ausência de rotas OIPv6. Habilite OSPFv3 e RID 32-bit válido. Hello v2 e passive v2 não carregam o plano IPv6.

sintoma: NOC-3401: design pedia R1 como Active do VIP 10.40.0.1; na prática R2 encaminha e R1 está Standby.
cli_output:
R1# show standby brief
                     P indicates configured to preempt.
Interface   Grp  Pri P State   Active          Standby         Virtual IP
Vl40        40   90    Standby 10.40.0.3       local           10.40.0.1

R2# show standby brief
Interface   Grp  Pri P State   Active          Standby         Virtual IP
Vl40        40  100    Active  local           10.40.0.2       10.40.0.1

R1# show run interface Vlan40 | include standby
 standby 40 ip 10.40.0.1
 standby 40 priority 90
 standby 40 preempt

R2# show run interface Vlan40 | include standby
 standby 40 ip 10.40.0.1
 standby 40 priority 100

Design: R1 should be preferred Active
alternativas: Priority de R1 (90) menor que R2 (100) — Active no router ‘errado’; subir priority em R1
explicacao_profunda: show standby brief: R2 Active com Pri 100 e R1 Standby com 90. Preempt em R1 não vence priority menor. Ajuste R1 para priority 110+ (e preempt). Grupo e VIP já batem.

sintoma: NOC-3402: após manutenção, R1 (preferido) voltou up mas o tráfego continua no R2; operadores querem R1 Active de novo.
cli_output:
R1# show standby brief
Interface   Grp  Pri P State   Active          Standby         Virtual IP
Vl40        40  120    Standby 10.40.0.3       local           10.40.0.1

R2# show standby brief
Interface   Grp  Pri P State   Active          Standby         Virtual IP
Vl40        40  100    Active  local           10.40.0.2       10.40.0.1

R1# show run interface Vlan40 | include standby
 standby 40 ip 10.40.0.1
 standby 40 priority 120
 (no preempt)

R2# show run interface Vlan40 | include standby
 standby 40 ip 10.40.0.1
 standby 40 priority 100

Timeline: R1 was reloaded; R2 became Active; R1 is back with higher priority
alternativas: Falta standby preempt em R1 — sem preempt o Active atual (R2) permanece apesar da priority maior em R1
explicacao_profunda: R1 tem Pri 120 mas sem P/preempt e fica Standby; R2 Active com 100. Habilite standby 40 preempt no R1 para reconquistar Active. VIP/grupo ok.

cli_output:
R1# show standby Vlan40
Vlan40 - Group 40
  State is Active
  Virtual IP address is 10.40.0.1
  Active router is local
  Standby router is unknown

R2# show standby Vlan40
Vlan40 - Group 41
  State is Active
  Virtual IP address is 10.40.0.1
  Active router is local
  Standby router is unknown

R1# show run interface Vlan40 | include standby
 standby 40 ip 10.40.0.1

 standby 40 preempt

R2# show run interface Vlan40 | include standby
 standby 41 ip 10.40.0.1
 standby 41 priority 100

Both SVIs up/up; L2 between cores OK per ops

explicacao_profunda: Grupo 40 vs 41 com Standby unknown = peers não se veem no mesmo grupo. Corrija standby 40 (ou 41) nos dois com o mesmo VIP. Priority/preempt secundários até o grupo casar.

sintoma: NOC-3404: um router de borda caiu e toda a VLAN perdeu Internet; só havia um gateway físico no DHCP.
cli_output:
PC> ipconfig
   IPv4 Address. . . . . . . . . . . : 10.40.0.55
   Default Gateway . . . . . . . . . : 10.40.0.2

R1# show run interface Vlan40
interface Vlan40
 ip address 10.40.0.2 255.255.255.0
 (no standby commands)

R2# show run interface Vlan40
interface Vlan40
 ip address 10.40.0.3 255.255.255.0
 (no standby commands)

R1# show standby brief
% No Hot Standby groups configured

R1 down during incident → PC gateway 10.40.0.2 unreachable
R2 was up but hosts do not use 10.40.0.3
alternativas: HSRP já está Active em ambos
Sem FHRP: gateway único 10.40.0.2 = SPOF — configurar HSRP VIP (ex. .1) nos dois e DHCP default-router = VIP
explicacao_profunda: Sem standby e com DHCP apontando ao IP físico do R1, a queda do R1 isola os hosts apesar do R2 up. Configure HSRP e mude o gateway dos hosts para o VIP.

sintoma: NOC-3405: HSRP não estabiliza; show standby fica em Speak/Init; VIP não responde ping.
cli_output:
R1# show standby Vlan40
Vlan40 - Group 40
  State is Speak
  Virtual IP address is 10.40.0.1
  Active router is unknown
  Standby router is unknown
  Priority 100 (default)

R1# show ip interface brief | include Vlan40
Vlan40   10.40.0.2   YES NVRAM  up   down

R1# show run interface Vlan40 | include standby|ip address
 ip address 10.40.0.2 255.255.255.0
 standby 40 ip 10.40.0.1

R2# show standby brief
Vl40  40  100  Active  local  unknown  10.40.0.1

R2 Vlan40 is up/up; R1 Vlan40 line protocol down (L2/VLAN issue on R1 side)
Log R1: %LINEPROTO-5-UPDOWN: Line protocol on Interface Vlan40, changed state to down
alternativas: SVI R1 up/down (line protocol down) — HSRP não completa; corrigir L2/VLAN no R1 para o grupo estabilizar
explicacao_profunda: Speak com Active unknown e Vlan40 up/down no R1 mostram falha de interface/L2, não só priority. R2 pode ficar Active sozinho; R1 não forma Standby saudável até o SVI ficar up/up. Corrija VLAN/trunk no lado R1.
